newsitem.title: UK: Dieting makes teenage girls miserable, study finds.
newsitem.headline: Dieting makes teenage girls miserable, study finds.

text.p: Adolescence, a miserable time for many girls, is even more depressing if they try to diet, two Australian researchers reported on Thursday.
Wendy Roncolato and Gail Huon of the University of New South Wales said two studies confirmed what many parents already knew -- that dieting made girls unhappy.

A survey of 83 girls with an average age of nearly 17 showed that, as expected, the dieters were more miserable than the non-dieters, the researchers told a meeting of the British Psychological Society.
A second survey five weeks later confirmed that the harder a girl found it to lose weight, the more unhappy she became.
In another study, they surveyed 27 consistent dieters over three months and found those who had trouble losing weight became increasingly miserable.

"Our efforts would be best directed toward improving adolescent girls' body-esteem and general happiness in order to reduce the likelihood of their taking up dieting in the first place," they recommended.

Other studies have found that girls as young as nine claim to be on diets to get thinner. Many researchers blame the prevalence of thin models on television and in newspapers and magazines and say they create an unhealthy and unrealistic ideal of beauty.
